title: Southeast Asia: renewable share fell in 10 of 11 countries

voiceover.text: In nineteen ninety, Vietnam ran on seventy-six percent renewable energy.
And it's not just Vietnam. Ten of eleven Southeast Asian countries fell.
Indonesia, fifty-nine to twenty. Laos, eighty-eight to fifty-two.
The only one that rose? Singapore. From almost zero, to one percent.
But this isn't a green story gone wrong.
Much of that renewable energy was firewood and charcoal.
As homes got electricity, the share fell. Power use per person grew twenty-four times.
So can a country use more power, and get greener at the same time?
Malaysia hit two percent in twenty ten. By twenty twenty-one, seven and a half, while power use kept climbing.
And Thailand? Nineteen percent. Its lowest since nineteen ninety.
We found this by joining three open datasets on Querious, right in your browser.
Filter to Southeast Asia, compare two years, then download the result.
The data is open. The question is yours.
